source_text:
3.23 Ἀντιπαθὲς
εὐπόριστον· τοῦ αὐτοῦ Πηγάνου φύλλα κʹ, κάρυα βασιλικὰ βʹ, ἁλὸς χόνδρον αʹ,
ἰσχάδας βʹ νήστει ἵππῳ προδιδοὺς ἐν ἐγχυματισμῷ ὑπ' οὐδενὸς φαρμάκου ἢ ἄλλου
τινὸς ἰοβόλου κακωθήσεσθαι ἐργάσῃ. Εἰς δὲ τὸ μὴ δηχθῆναι ὑπὸ σκορπίου εἰς
κασσιτέρινον πέταλον ἐπίγραψον· «ἀββάς», καὶ περιδέσμει τοῦτο τῷ τραχήλῳ τοῦ
ζῴου.
pass_a_gloss: 3.23 Antipathic easy-to-get: of-the-same. Of-rue leaves 20, walnuts royal 2, of-salt a-grain 1, dried-figs 2 to-a-fasting horse giving-first in a-drench by nothing of-a-drug or other some venomous to-be-harmed you-will-make. Into but the not to-be-bitten by a-scorpion into a-tin plate write: 'abbas', and bind-around this to-the-neck of-the-animal.
pass_b_english: An easy-to-get antipathic: of the same. Twenty leaves of rue, two royal walnuts, one grain of salt, two dried figs: giving these first to a fasting horse in a drench, you will make it be harmed by no drug or any other venomous thing. And toward not being bitten by a scorpion, write on a tin plate: “abbas,” and bind this around the neck of the animal.

choices.why: The lock's inscribed word on the tin plate, not translated as 'father' or expanded to a sentence.

anf_compare.notes: No PD English of the Cesti body; ANF has the letters only.
